Performance and accessibility are not paid extras. Every site we ship is built to load quickly on Australian mobile networks, work with screen readers and keyboards, and hold up under Google's Core Web Vitals. Our own site is the test bed: devarko.com scores 97 to 99 for performance and 100 for SEO on Lighthouse, and we hold client work to the same standard.

Speed matters commercially, not just technically. A slow site costs you rankings and enquiries before anyone reads a word. That is why our [SEO service](/seo-services/) and our development work share the same foundations: clean markup, fast loads and pages Google can read without guessing.

Every project starts with a conversation, not a form. We work out what the site or application actually needs to do, write it down in plain language, and quote against that scope. Time zones help rather than hurt. Lahore mornings line up with Australian afternoons, so calls, demos and urgent fixes happen inside your business hours. You will not be emailing into the void and waiting a full day for every answer.

h1: SEO services for Australian businesses, run by engineers
lede: Devarko is a software house headquartered in Australia, and our SEO work starts where most agencies stop: in the code. We fix the engineering problems that hold sites back in search, then write content aimed at the searches your buyers actually make. No ranking guarantees, no padded reports, and every result measured against your own Search Console data.

sections.h2: Technical SEO done by the people who build websites
paragraphs: Most SEO agencies write an audit, hand it to whoever looks after your website and hope for the best. Devarko is a software house first, so the people diagnosing your site are the same engineers who build platforms in Next.js, React and Laravel for a living. When we find a rendering issue or a crawl trap, we fix it in the code rather than writing a ticket someone else ignores.

That matters because Google rewards sites that load fast and behave predictably. Core Web Vitals, structured data and clean crawlability are engineering problems, and treating them as marketing problems is why so many audits go nowhere. If your current provider keeps sending PDF reports while nothing changes on the site, that is the gap we close.

bullets.title: Core Web Vitals
bullets.desc: Load speed, interactivity and layout stability tuned in the code itself, not patched over with another plugin.

bullets.title: Structured data
bullets.desc: Schema markup for your organisation, services, products and reviews, validated against Google's own testing tools.

bullets.title: Crawlability and indexing
bullets.desc: Clean sitemaps, sensible robots rules, canonical tags and redirect hygiene so Google spends its crawl budget on pages that earn money.

bullets.title: Site architecture
bullets.desc: URLs and internal links organised around how buyers search, so authority flows to the pages that convert.

sections.h2: Content aimed at buyer searches, not vanity keywords
paragraphs: Rankings are worthless if the keywords never turn into enquiries. We prioritise buyer searches: the terms people use when they are ready to compare providers, request quotes or purchase. That usually means fewer articles than a content-mill agency would sell you, written more carefully, mapped to pages that can convert.

Every piece starts with search data for your market in Australia, not a template. We write service pages, comparison pages and guides that answer the questions your customers ask before they buy, and we structure them so search engines can parse them properly.

Nobody controls Google, including the agencies that promise page one in 30 days. A guarantee either hides easy targets nobody searches for, or it relies on tactics that work briefly and then get your site penalised. When a provider guarantees rankings, they are telling you something about their honesty, not their skill.

What we commit to instead is the work and the evidence. You will see exactly what changed on your site, why it changed, and what happened in Search Console afterwards. Over six to twelve months that compounds into rankings that hold, because they are earned rather than gamed.

SEO takes time to show in revenue, but the first three months should never be quiet, and you should never be wondering what you paid for. Here is the sequence we follow on every engagement, so you can hold us to it from day one.

bullets.title: Weeks 1 to 2
bullets.desc: Access and baselines. We connect Search Console and analytics, record current rankings, traffic and indexing, and run a full technical crawl.

bullets.title: Weeks 3 to 6
bullets.desc: Technical fixes ship. Core Web Vitals, indexing problems and structured data get corrected in the code, not parked in a recommendations deck.

bullets.title: Weeks 7 to 10
bullets.desc: Keyword mapping against buyer intent, then the first round of new and rewritten pages goes live.

bullets.title: Weeks 11 to 13
bullets.desc: First review against the baseline: what moved, what has not yet, and the plan for the next quarter, in writing.

sections.h2: Measured against a Search Console baseline
paragraphs: Before we change anything, we record where you stand: impressions, clicks, average position for the queries that matter, and which pages Google has indexed. Every monthly report compares against that baseline, using your own Search Console data. You can verify every number yourself, which is exactly the point.

We report on enquiries and conversions where tracking allows, not just positions. A ranking that produces no phone calls is a decoration. If something we tried is not working, the report says so, along with what we are changing in response.
